name: Knappenwelt Gurgltal Tarrenz
kurzbeschreibung: Knappenwelt Gurgltal in Tarrenz: an authentically reconstructed 15th-century mining village featuring ore processing and a healer's herb garden.
beschreibung:
Overview

Knappenwelt Gurgltal is idyllically situated at the foot of the Tschirgant mountain in the hamlet of Strad, part of the municipality of Tarrenz near Imst in the Tiroler Oberland at an altitude of approximately 840 metres. Opened in 2008, this expansive open-air museum is an authentically reconstructed medieval mining village and is regarded as an outstanding monument to Tyrolean mining history. It provides a vivid impression of the heyday of Tyrolean ore extraction in the 15th and 16th centuries, when the Gurgltal valley ranked among the most important lead-mining centres in all of Europe, supplying valuable raw materials to the Fugger merchant dynasty and the Habsburg rulers.

Historic Mining Village & Healer's House

Knappenwelt consists of nine timber and stone buildings faithfully erected according to historical blueprints, linked together by narrow paths and watercourses. Visitors can tour the blacksmith's workshop, the miners' house with authentically furnished sleeping quarters, the pit clerk's office, the ore processing plant with a fully functional wooden stamping mill, and an authentically replicated mining tunnel. Engaging multimedia stations and audio guides (including a special children's trail) depict the arduous and dangerous daily life of the miners underground. A major highlight is the Haus der Heilerin (House of the Healer): inspired by the bestselling historical novel "The Wandering Harlot" (Die Wanderhure) by Iny Lorentz—for whose television adaptation Knappenwelt served as an authentic film set—the exhibition illuminates medieval monastic medicine and herbal remedies. In the adjoining Kräutergarten (herb garden), over 100 alpine medicinal and poisonous plants grow, which were used by medieval miners to treat wounds and alleviate mining ailments.

Visit & Getting There

Knappenwelt Gurgltal is open from early May to late October from Tuesday to Sunday between 10:00 and 17:00 (closed Mondays; open daily in July and August). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €9.50, seniors approx. €8.50, children and youth (ages 6 to 15) approx. €5.00, young children under 6 free; family ticket approx. €22.00. Holders of the regional Urlaubspass Imst enjoy discounted admission. Travelling by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 to Imst, then take the B189 towards Nassereith/Fernpass to Tarrenz, district of Strad; ample free parking is available directly at Knappenwelt 1. By public transport: ÖBB train to Imst-Pitztal railway station, from where VVT bus line 4206 or 4208 runs every half hour to the Tarrenz Strad stop (around a five-minute walk to the entrance).

Tips

The entire open-air museum grounds are largely flat and easily accessible with pushchairs and all-terrain wheelchairs; handcarts can be rented for children at the ticket desk. Younger visitors love the gold- and mineral-panning stations, where they can wash genuine pyrites and semi-precious stones from the gravel using sieves. The historic tavern Happis Hütte right on the museum grounds serves traditional Tyrolean miners' skillets and refreshments.
